page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by a 35 MB L3 cache. It includes 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6870.73 and a Passmark CPU score of 7626.07. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1304.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1155.0. Memory bandwidth is solid, achieving an average read-only small block speed of 382.09 GB/sec and large block write speeds of 40.38 GB/sec. Database operations and text processing show mixed results, with Redis SET operations performing at an average of 6.38 million operations per second, while Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput are categorized as weak. LLM inference capabilities are limited, showing poor performance on medium 7B models.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 and bundled high-speed NVMe local storage, the r5dn.2xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for memory-intensive applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial RAM and fast local temporary storage without needing massive compute scaling. This instance is well-suited for memory-cached databases, Redis deployments, data buffering, and moderate-scale enterprise applications that benefit from network and EBS optimization alongside local NVMe storage.
